name: trader
why: Star Traders is an old-school space trading game, the kind of strange terminal game worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: Star Traders is a simple text-based game of interstellar trading, played on a terminal. Players create companies, buy and sell shares, and borrow and repay money, with the aim of becoming the wealthiest player. It is written in C and runs on modern Unix-like systems with a C99 compiler, and the homepage says it can run in sixteen human languages. Its historical versions were released for MBASIC, CP/M-80, CP/M-86, MS-DOS, Windows 3.1 and the Commodore 64.
brief.why_it_exists: It is a revival of a 1977 microcomputer game, Star Lanes, which the author describes as a Monopoly-type game combining financial and positional strategy. The author frames the project as preserving that history: 'Now you, too, can run this small piece of computing history!'
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals beyond saying the current version is rewritten in C and that the original algorithms were carried through earlier rewrites. Gameplay runs in a text terminal. The author notes the screenshot was taken on a VT420 terminal attached to Linux over RS232 serial.

commands_seen.context: Downloads the self-contained AppImage build of the current version, with -N to fetch only if newer.
Runs the game from the AppImage.

brief.install_notes: Options from the homepage: the AppImage (download, chmod a+x, run) for most Linux systems; precompiled packages for Debian, Ubuntu, CentOS, Fedora, OpenSUSE, Mageia, macOS and Cygwin; an APT repository for Debian and Ubuntu; or building from source (tar.xz or tar.gz, with GnuPG signatures) using the prerequisites listed in the INSTALL.pdf file. The homepage says INSTALL.pdf does not contain generic GNU Autoconf instructions. No accounts, hardware or first-run configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: It is a faithful lineage piece: the same game has been rebuilt for CP/M, MS-DOS, Windows 3.1, and the Commodore 64, with the author documenting each step. The homepage also includes screenshots of the game on a real 1990s VT420 terminal over serial.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows. The current version is 7.21, the copyright runs to 2026, the source is in a public git repository, and there are historical and translation pages. The homepage gives no exact date for the 7.21 release, so the last release date is unknown.
brief.caveats: Building from source needs a C99 compiler and the prerequisites in INSTALL.pdf. The AppImage filename indicates x86_64 Linux only. The homepage lists Linux, macOS, FreeBSD and Cygwin as supported Unix-like systems. The historical versions are retro builds, not updated versions. The Homebrew entry has no caveats, and the scout note's 'strange terminal game' framing is the scout's, not the author's.
quotes: Star Traders is a simple text-based game of interstellar trading, where the objective is to create companies, buy and sell shares, borrow and repay money, in order to become the wealthiest player (the winner).
Historical versions of Star Traders are also available for your nostalgic download pleasure…
Now you, too, can run this small piece of computing history!
fetch_log: https://www.zap.org.au/projects/trader/ - fetched successfully; the homepage contains the full description, download notes, history, screenshots and copyright. It is not a GitHub repository, and the page was detailed enough that I did not follow further links.
